messages.author: beef5979959ede57
messages.subject: colours
parts:
Dear All - I'm a new user of ggplot and have what must be a very simple question about applying colours:

For example, the following is a  boxplot:

Sitebox<-ggplot(wasps,aes(tmnt1,wing))+geom_boxplot()

tmnt1 has 4 levels, so I get 4 boxplots on the same graph. Fine.

But I'd also like to have different fill colours for the boxes.

From looking under the online reference manual under geom_boxplot, it seems that the following should produce a different colour for each box:

Sitebox<-ggplot(wasps,aes(tmnt1,wing))+geom_boxplot(aes(fill = tmnt1))
Sitebox
Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'digest'

Is there a library I need to load?

However, what I'd really like to do is have a black (or dark grey - so that the median line is still visible) fill for 2 of the boxplots (the 2nd & 4th ones), and leave the 1st and 3rd ones unfilled, as above.

I've also tried looking in the ggplot book, scale_colour_manual etc, but can't get it to work, e.g.:

colours<-c(FromNorth ="red", FromSouth ="blue", NorthNatives ="green", SouthNatives ="yellow")
#these are the 4 levels in tmnt1
Col<-Sitebox+aes(colour=tmnt1)+scale_colour_manual(values=colours)
Col
Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'digest'


Any advice?

Jeremy Field
University of Sussex,
Falmer,
Brighton BN1 9QG, UK

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: colours
parts:
> Sitebox<-ggplot(wasps,aes(tmnt1,wing))+geom_boxplot(aes(fill = tmnt1))
> Sitebox
> Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'digest'

This suggests something has gone wrong with your ggplot2 install. I'd
suggest checking that you have the latest version of R, re-installing
ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2")), then restarting R.

Hadley

parts:
Dear All - regarding my query of 11 October about 'colours' on the ggplot mailing list (I've put my original query at the end, below). Thanks very much for your detailed replies. I’m just trying them out. I've just done what Hadley Wickham suggested (see below) and installed R 2.13.2 (previously I had 12.2) so i can get the latest ggplot2. However, when I then type:

install.packages("ggplot2")

as he suggested, I get:

Warning: unable to access index for repository http://www.sourcekeg.co.uk/cran/bin/macosx/leopard/contrib/2.13
Warning message:
In getDependencies(pkgs, dependencies, available, lib) :
  package ‘ggplot2’ is not available (for R version 2.13.2)

I get the same error if I try installing anything else e.g. the lme4 package. I remember now that the same thing happened when I'd just installed version 2.12. I expect I can get ggplot2, lme 4 et al. another way, but I'm just wondering if this is why I had the problem with using colours in ggplot - I must have ended up getting ggplot2 manually somehow, maybe by downloading it directly from the ggplot website, hence perhaps not getting the 'digest' package automatically??

Not having used R itself for that long, I don't suppose any of you knows what I need to do to get ‘install.packages’ to work, as it would obviously be generally useful to do so? (I have Mac OS 10.6.6 by the way).

 

Many thanks,

Jeremy Field
